knowledge_point.title: Computing the Volume of a Region Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Find the volume bounded by the region $R,$ given by

$$
R=\big\{(x,y,z)\, :\, 0\le 3 x\le 6,\quad 0\le 2 x + y\le 3,\quad 0\le 3 z\le 5\big\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
0\le 3 x\le 6,\quad 0\le 2 x + y\le 3,\quad 0\le 3 z\le 5,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=3 x,\quad v=2 x + y,\quad w=3 z.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
T^{-1}:(x,y,z)\longmapsto(u(x,y,z),v(x,y,z),w(x,y,z)).
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\big\{(u,v,w):0\le u\le 6,\quad 0\le v\le 3,\quad 0\le w\le 5\big\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(3\right)(-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{9}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

The map to $R$ is

$$
T(u,v,w)=\left(\frac{u}{3},- \frac{2 u}{3} + v,\frac{w}{3}\right).
$$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta 1\cdot |\frac{1}{9}|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{0}^{6}\int_{0}^{3}\int_{0}^{5}\frac{1}{9}\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot \int_{0}^{6}1\,\mathrm{d}u\cdot \int_{0}^{3}1\,\mathrm{d}v\cdot \int_{0}^{5}1\,\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot [u]_{0}^{6}\cdot [v]_{0}^{3}\cdot [w]_{0}^{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot \left(\left(\left(6\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\left(3\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\left(5\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\cdot \left(\left(6\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(3\right)-\left(0\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(5\right)-\left(0\right)\right) \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Computing the Volume of a Region Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Find the volume bounded by the region $R,$ given by

$$
R=\big\{(x,y,z)\, :\, -1\le 3 x + 3 y\le 4,\quad -1\le 3 x - y\le 3,\quad 1\le z^{3}\le 8\big\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
-1\le 3 x + 3 y\le 4,\quad -1\le 3 x - y\le 3,\quad 1\le z^{3}\le 8,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=3 x + 3 y,\quad v=3 x - y,\quad w=z^{3}.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
T^{-1}:(x,y,z)\longmapsto(u(x,y,z),v(x,y,z),w(x,y,z)).
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\big\{(u,v,w):-1\le u\le 4,\quad -1\le v\le 3,\quad 1\le w\le 8\big\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}3 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 z^{2}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(3\right)(-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 z^{2}\end{vmatrix}+\left(3\right)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 z^{2}\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =- 36 z^{2} \\  & =- 36 w^{\frac{2}{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=- \frac{1}{36 w^{\frac{2}{3}}}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

The map to $R$ is

$$
T(u,v,w)=\left(\frac{u}{12} + \frac{v}{4},\frac{u}{4} - \frac{v}{4},\sqrt[3]{w}\right).
$$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta 1\cdot |- \frac{1}{36 w^{\frac{2}{3}}}|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{-1}^{4}\int_{-1}^{3}\int_{1}^{8}\frac{1}{36 w^{\frac{2}{3}}}\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =1\cdot \int_{-1}^{4}1\,\mathrm{d}u\cdot \int_{-1}^{3}1\,\mathrm{d}v\cdot \int_{1}^{8}\frac{1}{36 w^{\frac{2}{3}}}\,\mathrm{d}w \\  & =1\cdot [u]_{-1}^{4}\cdot [v]_{-1}^{3}\cdot [\frac{\sqrt[3]{w}}{12}]_{1}^{8} \\  & =1\cdot \left(\left(\left(4\right)\right)-\left(\left(-1\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\left(3\right)\right)-\left(\left(-1\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\frac{\sqrt[3]{\left(8\right)}}{12}\right)-\left(\frac{\sqrt[3]{\left(1\right)}}{12}\right)\right) \\  & =1\cdot \left(\left(4\right)-\left(-1\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(3\right)-\left(-1\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)-\left(\frac{1}{12}\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Computing the Volume of a Region Using a Change of Variables

question.:question/problem:
Find the volume bounded by the region $R,$ given by

$$
R=\big\{(x,y,z)\, :\, \frac{1}{2}\le x\le 3,\quad 1\le - 3 x^{2} + y\le 4,\quad 1\le 2 x z\le 6\big\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
\frac{1}{2}\le x\le 3,\quad 1\le - 3 x^{2} + y\le 4,\quad 1\le 2 x z\le 6,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=x,\quad v=- 3 x^{2} + y,\quad w=2 x z.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
T^{-1}:(x,y,z)\longmapsto(u(x,y,z),v(x,y,z),w(x,y,z)).
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\big\{(u,v,w):\frac{1}{2}\le u\le 3,\quad 1\le v\le 4,\quad 1\le w\le 6\big\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ - 6 x & 1 & 0 \\ 2 z & 0 & 2 x\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(1\right)(-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 x\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}- 6 x & 0 \\ 2 z & 2 x\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}- 6 x & 1 \\ 2 z & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =2 x \\  & =2 u\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{2 u}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

The map to $R$ is

$$
T(u,v,w)=\left(u,3 u^{2} + v,\frac{w}{2 u}\right).
$$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta 1\cdot |\frac{1}{2 u}|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^{3}\int_{1}^{4}\int_{1}^{6}\frac{1}{2 u}\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =1\cdot \int_{\frac{1}{2}}^{3}\frac{1}{2 u}\,\mathrm{d}u\cdot \int_{1}^{4}1\,\mathrm{d}v\cdot \int_{1}^{6}1\,\mathrm{d}w \\  & =1\cdot [\frac{\ln{\left(u \right)}}{2}]_{\frac{1}{2}}^{3}\cdot [v]_{1}^{4}\cdot [w]_{1}^{6} \\  & =1\cdot \left(\left(\frac{\ln{\left(\left(3\right) \right)}}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{\ln{\left(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \right)}}{2}\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\left(4\right)\right)-\left(\left(1\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\left(6\right)\right)-\left(\left(1\right)\right)\right) \\  & =1\cdot \left(\left(\frac{\ln{\left(3 \right)}}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{\ln{\left(2 \right)}}{2}\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(4\right)-\left(1\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(6\right)-\left(1\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{15 \ln{\left(6 \right)}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the volume bounded by the region $R,$ given by

$$
R=\big\{(x,y,z)\, :\, 1\le y\le 7,\quad 1\le x + \sqrt{y}\le 4,\quad 1\le \frac{1}{z - 3}\le 4\big\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
1\le y\le 7,\quad 1\le x + \sqrt{y}\le 4,\quad 1\le \frac{1}{z - 3}\le 4,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=y,\quad v=x + \sqrt{y},\quad w=\frac{1}{z - 3}.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
T^{-1}:(x,y,z)\longmapsto(u(x,y,z),v(x,y,z),w(x,y,z)).
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\big\{(u,v,w):1\le u\le 7,\quad 1\le v\le 4,\quad 1\le w\le 4\big\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{y}} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & - \frac{1}{\left(z - 3\right)^{2}}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{y}} & 0 \\ 0 & - \frac{1}{\left(z - 3\right)^{2}}\end{vmatrix}+\left(1\right)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & - \frac{1}{\left(z - 3\right)^{2}}\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}1 & \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{y}} \\ 0 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{\left(z - 3\right)^{2}} \\  & =w^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{w^{2}}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

The map to $R$ is

$$
T(u,v,w)=\left(- \sqrt{u} + v,u,3 + \frac{1}{w}\right).
$$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta 1\cdot |\frac{1}{w^{2}}|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{1}^{7}\int_{1}^{4}\int_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{w^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =1\cdot \int_{1}^{7}1\,\mathrm{d}u\cdot \int_{1}^{4}1\,\mathrm{d}v\cdot \int_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{w^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}w \\  & =1\cdot [u]_{1}^{7}\cdot [v]_{1}^{4}\cdot [- \frac{1}{w}]_{1}^{4} \\  & =1\cdot \left(\left(\left(7\right)\right)-\left(\left(1\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\left(4\right)\right)-\left(\left(1\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(- \frac{1}{\left(4\right)}\right)-\left(- \frac{1}{\left(1\right)}\right)\right) \\  & =1\cdot \left(\left(7\right)-\left(1\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(4\right)-\left(1\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(- \frac{1}{4}\right)-\left(-1\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{27}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the volume bounded by the region $R,$ given by

$$
R=\big\{(x,y,z)\, :\, 2\le x\le 8,\quad 1\le - 3 x^{2} - y - 2 z\le 4,\quad 1\le \sqrt{z}\le 4\big\}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
2\le x\le 8,\quad 1\le - 3 x^{2} - y - 2 z\le 4,\quad 1\le \sqrt{z}\le 4,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=x,\quad v=- 3 x^{2} - y - 2 z,\quad w=\sqrt{z}.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
T^{-1}:(x,y,z)\longmapsto(u(x,y,z),v(x,y,z),w(x,y,z)).
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\big\{(u,v,w):2\le u\le 8,\quad 1\le v\le 4,\quad 1\le w\le 4\big\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ - 6 x & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{z}}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(1\right)(-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}-1 & -2 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{z}}\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}- 6 x & -2 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{z}}\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}- 6 x & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =- \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{z}} \\  & =- \frac{1}{2 w}\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=- 2 w.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

The map to $R$ is

$$
T(u,v,w)=\left(u,- 3 u^{2} - v - 2 w^{2},w^{2}\right).
$$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta 1\cdot |- 2 w|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{2}^{8}\int_{1}^{4}\int_{1}^{4}2 w\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =1\cdot \int_{2}^{8}1\,\mathrm{d}u\cdot \int_{1}^{4}1\,\mathrm{d}v\cdot \int_{1}^{4}2 w\,\mathrm{d}w \\  & =1\cdot [u]_{2}^{8}\cdot [v]_{1}^{4}\cdot [w^{2}]_{1}^{4} \\  & =1\cdot \left(\left(\left(8\right)\right)-\left(\left(2\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\left(4\right)\right)-\left(\left(1\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\left(4\right)^{2}\right)-\left(\left(1\right)^{2}\right)\right) \\  & =1\cdot \left(\left(8\right)-\left(2\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(4\right)-\left(1\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(16\right)-\left(1\right)\right) \\  & =270\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v \\ w\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{bmatrix}
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
2\le - 3 x + 2 z\le 8,\quad 1\le y\le 4,\quad 2\le - 3 y + 2 z\le 7,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=- 3 x + 2 z,\quad v=y,\quad w=- 3 y + 2 z.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
T^{-1}:(x,y,z)\longmapsto(u(x,y,z),v(x,y,z),w(x,y,z)).
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\big\{(u,v,w):2\le u\le 8,\quad 1\le v\le 4,\quad 2\le w\le 7\big\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(-3\right)(-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -3 & 2\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{vmatrix}+\left(2\right)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=- \frac{1}{6}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

The map to $R$ is

$$
T(u,v,w)=\left(- \frac{u}{3} + v + \frac{w}{3},v,\frac{3 v}{2} + \frac{w}{2}\right).
$$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iiint_R\mathrm{d}V & =\iiint_\Delta 1\cdot |- \frac{1}{6}|\,\mathrm{d}u\mathrm{d}v\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\int_{2}^{8}\int_{1}^{4}\int_{2}^{7}\frac{1}{6}\,\mathrm{d}w\,\mathrm{d}v\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot \int_{2}^{8}1\,\mathrm{d}u\cdot \int_{1}^{4}1\,\mathrm{d}v\cdot \int_{2}^{7}1\,\mathrm{d}w \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot [u]_{2}^{8}\cdot [v]_{1}^{4}\cdot [w]_{2}^{7} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot \left(\left(\left(8\right)\right)-\left(\left(2\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\left(4\right)\right)-\left(\left(1\right)\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(\left(7\right)\right)-\left(\left(2\right)\right)\right) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot \left(\left(8\right)-\left(2\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(4\right)-\left(1\right)\right)\cdot \left(\left(7\right)-\left(2\right)\right) \\  & =15\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\Delta=\big\{(u,v,w):2\le u\le 7,\quad -2\le v\le 2,\quad -1\le w\le 1\big\}.
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left(1\right)(-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}-3 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+2}\begin{vmatrix}0 & 2 \\ 0 & -1\end{vmatrix}+\left(0\right)(-1)^{1+3}\begin{vmatrix}0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =1\end{aligned}

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}=1.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

The map to $R$ is

$$
T(u,v,w)=\left(u,- v - 2 w,- v - 3 w\right).
